### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events of A10 and A11 was about 1.0 hour on average (median about 1.0 hour; the middle half of intervals between roughly 0.90 and 1.11 hours). In the later window it is about 0.5 hour (median about 0.49 hour; middle half between roughly 0.44 and 0.55 hours) — a drop of about half an hour, roughly halving the interval. [TWAIT001]
- The intervals also became more uniform: the spread halved from a standard deviation of about 0.16 hours to about 0.08 hours. [TWAIT001]
- How often this pair of consecutive completions occurred barely changed: about 330 intervals in the earlier window versus about 344 in the later one, roughly 1.7 per trace in both windows of 200 traces. [TWAIT001]
- No control-flow difference passed screening (0 of 46 units, against about 0.23 expected by chance), so no structural change was detected; this timing item was the only qualifying evidence overall. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a timing change as a possibility: in the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A10 and A11 is about half of what it was in the earlier window, falling from about 1.0 hour to about 0.5 hour per interval, with the variability halving as well. The change is measured directly on this activity pair, is consistent across every distribution component (mean, median and both quartiles each fell by about 0.5 hours), rests on many observations (about 330 versus 344 intervals), and is larger than in about 1999 out of 2000 random re-splits; the time family produced 1 qualifying item where about 0.006 would be expected if nothing had changed. No control-flow items qualified, so this stands as a pure timing change, which needs no structural counterpart. [TWAIT001]

Limitation: TWAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting or processing time, so the evidence cannot distinguish whether A10 and A11 were completed faster themselves or whether the time between the two completions (for example queueing or batching) shrank; a shift in the mix of cases reaching this pair also cannot be fully excluded, although the uniform shift makes plain sampling variation unlikely. [TWAIT001]

Other differences: none — no other indicator passed the configured thresholds. [TWAIT001]
